hypotheses.justification: The definitions involved are `chiMK κ m k t x = (-(I.corrTime κ m k t)) • uShear β I.Λ m k x` and `uShear β Λ m k x = if k % 4 = 1 then ![0, …] else if k % 4 = 3 then ![-(…cos(2π x 1/ε)), 0] else 0`. So the statement still holds when k % 4 ≠ 3, and the proof splits on `k % 4 = 3`. If it holds, the existing proof applies unchanged. If it does not, component 0 of `uShear β I.Λ m k y` is 0 for every y: in the branch k % 4 = 1 it is `![0, …] 0 = 0`, and otherwise the value is `0`. Hence `fun y => I.chiMK κ m k t y 0` is the constant function 0, provable by `funext y; simp [Ingredients.chiMK, uShear, hk]` together with a split on `k % 4 = 1`. Then the left side is 0: `spaceLap f x = ∑ i, spaceGrad (fun y => spaceGrad f y i) x i` and `spaceGrad f x i = fderiv ℝ f x (basisVec i)`. The fderiv of a constant function is 0 (`fderiv_const`/`fderiv_zero`), so the inner gradient is the constant 0 and so is the outer one. The right side is `-(4π²/ε²) * I.chiMK κ m k t x 0 = -(4π²/ε²) * 0 = 0`. The ε = 0 junk case does not matter, since everything is multiplied by 0. Both sides are 0, so the theorem holds for every k.
